The authors consider a pressure-driven microchannel flow of a power-law fluid with constant but unequal heat fluxes imposed at the upper and lower walls.
The slip coefficients on the upper and lower walls are denoted as K1 and K2, respectively, allowing for asymmetric slip.
The authors derive exact analytical expressions for the velocity profile, temperature distribution, and entropy generation rate in the microchannel.
Asymmetric slip shifts the location of the maximum velocity towards the wall with larger slip coefficient.
Asymmetric slip enhances the fluid momentum and thermal energy fluxes along the wall with larger slip, improving heat transfer.
The Bejan number profile shows a sharp transition between entropy generation due to heat transfer and due to fluid flow at an off-center location under asymmetric slip.
For shear-thinning fluids (n < 1), irreversibility is primarily due to fluid friction, while for shear-thickening fluids (n > 1), it is primarily due to heat transfer.
The modified Brinkman number Br' for power-law fluids is defined as Br' = (V_c q_1) / (H^(n+1) a).
The Hatzikiriakos slip law predicts a higher Nusselt number and less entropy generation compared to the asymptotic slip law for the same slip coefficient.
Asymmetric slip promotes uniformity in both the velocity and temperature fields, thereby reducing irreversibility in the flow.
The difference in imposed heat fluxes leads to different Bejan number profiles depending on which wall is hotter and the fluid's shear behavior.
The authors consider power-law index values of n = 0.5 (shear-thinning) and n = 1.5 (shear-thickening) in their analysis.
The dimensionless slip coefficients on the upper and lower walls are set to K1 = 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25 and K2 = 1.0, respectively.
The dimensionless heat flux ratio q2/q1 is considered to be 0.5 and 2.0 in the analysis.
The Brinkman number Br' is kept constant at 0.2 in the presented results.
